Existing positional callers (6 args) must not break on the new field.
DCP shards a replicated group's objects on the server (its ``ShardReplicationDesc``); the kv rank space stays one rank per worker.
One attention block id spans block_size * dcp global tokens.
Recurrent state is replicated per rank, so its span is unchanged.
No DCP means no scaling anywhere -- the legacy path is untouched.
MLA + KDA at block 1024, dcp 2 -> [2048, 1024]; LCM alignment 2048.
Workers adjust the interleave, the scheduler does not; names must match.
Without DCP, even otherwise-rejected settings must not raise.
PP + DCP is supported: each pipeline stage has its own TP ranks, sharded by DCP among them.
Opaque per-rank pages round-trip when their key namespace is isolated.
The resolved 2304 page, rather than the CLI 256 page, is authoritative.
Ranks split into contiguous per-server blocks; a block of a multiple of dcp_size ranks holds whole shard sets, so each server is independently servable.
TP8 across 2 servers leaves 4 ranks each, which cannot hold 8 shards. Lookup takes the min across servers, so a partial server reports 0 hits.
TP6 across 2 servers leaves 3 ranks each: shard 0 twice and shard 1 once, so a rank's shard is no longer its position among the server's TP ranks.
The multi-server MLA path is unchanged when DCP is off.
Reproduces vLLM's contiguous group construction and asserts the server keys a replicated group's object by ``tp_rank % dcp_size``, the shard vLLM gives that rank; fails if upstream goes strided.
UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs derives from KVCacheSpec, not AttentionSpec; without unwrapping, wrapped attention groups skip DCP scaling.
Unwrapping must not turn a wrapped recurrent group into a scaled one.

Inside a UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs group, per-layer specs decide the window. SW layers with a distinct transfer identity get their own group carrying the window size.
Same-identity layers mixing different windows are inconsistent vLLM metadata and fail loudly.

per_layer_engine_group_idx must hold one entry per layer.
Same-shape pools sharing a block size fold into ONE group.
Different block sizes are different paged address spaces: no sharing.
tokens_per_block sizes each rank's memory object; unscaled it would be dcp times too large.
dcp_size defaults to 1, leaving every group exactly as before.
Scratch detection honors both marker versions, with the new one first.
Scratch groups cover no tokens: their layers form no info.
A scratch ring whose layout format discovery would reject must not block registration: its layers skip discovery and stay excluded.
A group whose spec declares full tensor-parallel replication (``max_tp_shards == 1``) carries the caller's replica count; any other group carries 1.
vLLM may put a sharded K+V layer and an MLA layer in one ``UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`` group. They split into separate kernel groups by tensor shape, and only the MLA kernel group is replicated.
An MLA spec that leaves ``max_tp_shards`` unset is still one latent head held in full on every TP rank, so it is tagged like a declared one.
Only full replication shares an object: a cache split into fewer shards than ranks is still stored per rank.
A model whose every layer is MLA has no sharded group: all of its KV is keyed once per TP group, sharded only by DCP.
